Where it began

Dale Steyn was born on 27 June 1983 in Phalaborwa, a small town right on the edge of the Kruger Park, into a family with roots in Zimbabwe. He first played first-class cricket for Northerns in October 2003, and a lively start to the following season put him in the Test side against England in December 2004.

His first wicket was Marcus Trescothick, bowled. Those early Tests were a hard education, and he went back to domestic cricket, worked on his game, including a spell with Essex, and returned to the Test team against New Zealand in 2006 with a five-wicket haul at Centurion.

The player

From there he barely looked back. Steyn played 93 Tests for South Africa between 2004 and 2019 and took 439 wickets at 22.95, with 26 five-wicket innings, five ten-wicket matches and a best of 7 for 51. Only ten men in Test history have taken more wickets.

The highlights come thick and fast. In the 2007–08 season he took 78 wickets, and he was named the best Test cricketer in the world for 2008. He took ten wickets in a Test, and made a fighting 76, to help South Africa to their first Test series win in Australia, and against Pakistan in 2013 he took 6 for 8 as they were bowled out for 49. In December 2018 he passed Shaun Pollock to become South Africa's leading Test wicket-taker.

What made him special

Plenty of bowlers are fast and plenty swing the ball. Steyn did both at once, regularly above 140 km/h, with the ball moving late, and with the old ball he could make it reverse on the deadest of pitches. At his peak he sat at the top of the world Test bowling rankings for a record 263 weeks. He reached 400 Test wickets in fewer balls than any bowler before him.

He bowled with obvious joy and celebrated each wicket as though it were his first. With the bat he was more of a hopeful visitor, with an average of 13.60, but he could dig in: that 76 in Australia came in a ninth-wicket stand of 180 with JP Duminy.

Away from the middle

Wisden named him its Leading Cricketer in the World for 2013, and he was later chosen among its cricketers of the decade. He played county cricket for Essex and Warwickshire and travelled the world's T20 leagues. After retiring from all cricket in August 2021 he became a bowling coach, with Sunrisers Hyderabad, Washington Freedom and Sunrisers Eastern Cape, who reached three SA20 finals under him and won two. He even turned up on the big screen, playing himself in the 2014 comedy Blended.

And finally

Steyn once said he simply wanted to be the quickest bowler in the world. Several hundred batsmen would confirm he got close enough.
